newsitem.title: USA: TransAmerican to go solo on refinery. [CORRECTED 08:55 GMT 08/03]
newsitem.headline: TransAmerican to go solo on refinery. [CORRECTED 08:55 GMT 08/03]

text.p: (Corrects to make clear that TransAmerican Natural Gas Corp is parent company of both TransTexas Gas Corp and TransAmerican Refining Corp.)
By Ransdell Pierson

TransAmerican Natural Gas Corp and its TransAmerican Refining Corp unit will finance a stalled $560 million upgrade of the unit's Louisiana refinery rather than rely on Petroleos de Venezuela and other potential partners, TransAmerican officials told Reuters. "We have committed to finish the construction with internal funds," Simon Ward said Friday. Ward is a spokesman for TransAmerican Natural Gas and TransAmerican Refining, its wholly-owned refining unit.

TransAmerican Refining's sole refinery is located near New Orleans in Good Hope, Louisiana. The upgrade would give the mothballed plant crude capacity of 200,000 barrels per day (bpd), making it a major player in the Gulf Coast refined products market.

Strapped for funds, the refinery laid off more than 65 percent of its construction work force last year, leaving about 450 workers on the job but with still more than half the reconstruction yet to be done.

Ward said TransAmerican Refining aims to complete the job by 1999, then recoup its investment over three years by processing cheaper heavy crudes expected to soon flood the market from increased production in Venezuela and the Gulf of Mexico.

"What we are talking about is not a low-margin refinery but one that maximizes value from each barrel of cheap feedstocks," he said, adding that a new 60,000 barrel-per-day "delayed coker" and a 120,000 bpd fluid catalytic cracker will be able to tackle the heavy crudes.

Ward confirmed TransAmerican Refining held talks with Petroleos de Venezuela SA and other companies in recent months about possible partnerships, but the parent company's own improving finances now allow it to proceed alone.
He noted the parent company's financial footing is much improved because another subsidiary, TransTexas Gas Corp, is making progress in its restructuring efforts.
He cited ongoing negotiations, announced last month, to sell the gas unit's Lobo Trend natgas properties for $1.1 billion to a major refiner, identified by others as Conoco Inc, a unit of DuPont Inc.
Ward also said TransTexas Gas is now producing 260 million cubic feet per day of natgas from its two-year-old Bob West North natural gas field near Laredo, Texas.
Although TransTexas is projecting healthier days, Wall Street analysts have deemed it highly leveraged for an independent producer.
Maraven, a unit of PDVSA, began talks with TransAmerican Refining last September, but is no longer mulling a partnership role, a Maraven official said.
"The refinery does not have a lot of priority. There has been no progress. PDVSA has better options," he said.
PDVSA is seeking partnership agreements with Gulf Coast refineries as a way of finding a home for its burgeoning production of heavy crude, expected to double over the next decade.
Coastal Corp and Phillips Petroleum have joint venture deals, while some of the refinery interests owned by Basis Petroleum, a unit of Salomon Bros, are seen as possible bid targets.
TransAmerican Refining last month said its bondholders had agreed to extend the Feb 15 completion date for the first phase of the Louisiana refinery upgrade until July 15.
Without the 11th-hour agreement, holders of $440 million in bonds issued in 1994 could have demanded full payment from the company.
TransAmerican Refining officials estimated $440 million is about what is needed to complete improvements at the refinery, which has a long and tangled history.
The parent company, TransAmerican Natural Gas, emerged from bankruptcy in 1987 and formed the TransAmerican Refining subsidiary, which in turn launched its current reconstruction program in 1993.
Production has been limited since then to between 40,000 and 60,000 barrels per day of vaccuum gas oil and No. 6 fuel oil from a vacuum unit.
"The unit has operated less than 40 percent of the time over the last 12 months," Ward said, adding it had been shut down recently because of ongoing construction.
- ((New York Energy Desk, 212 859-1632))
